memo: This memo summarises the April 2026 regional updates for the investment committee.
Thanks to Maria for pulling the three reports together.
Sub-Saharan Africa's growth is projected to remain at 4.1 percent in 2026.
That projection was revised down by 0.3 percentage points from October 2025.
A weaker U.S. dollar has eased inflationary pressures across the region.
High prices for coffee and cocoa boosted revenues in 2025.
Latin America and the Caribbean is projected to grow 2.1 percent in 2026.
Growth in the region was 2.4 percent in 2025.
Private consumption remains the main driver of growth there.
Tariffs on the region have risen more than expected.
Progress against inflation continues, but more slowly than expected.
I think the region's clean power mix is its best long-term asset.
South Asia's growth is expected to slow to 6.3 percent in 2026.
South Asia remains the fastest-growing EMDE region thanks to India.
South Asian countries use industrial policies at about three times the rate of other EMDEs.
Since 2022, about half of South Asia's industrial policies have targeted manufacturing.
Import restrictions in South Asia lowered imports significantly.
Export support in South Asia has not materially raised exports.
Should we revisit our allocation to oil-importing countries?
The conflict in the Middle East has raised Brent crude and liquefied natural gas prices.
Fertilizer prices have also increased.
We recommend holding the current allocation until the June updates.
In my view, the downside risks in Africa are understated.
Please send comments by Friday.
Can someone check the debt-service figures?
Let's discuss this at Tuesday's meeting.
